The change in the median consensus EPS estimate for FY1 from three months ago relative to the absolute value of the current median median consensus EPS estimate for FY1.  To limit the impact of small divisor, the factor is not calculated for firms with FY1 EPS less than 2 cents
This indicator is an equal weighted combination of the following momentum factors: PM12M1M, PM1M, HL1M, PM5D, PM9M.
This indicator is an equal weighted combination of the following historical growth factors: 1YChgAstAdjFCF, 1YChgAstAdjOCF, Chg1YAstTO, SusGrwRate, and Chg1YEPS.
This indicator is an equal weighted combination of the following capital efficiency factors: ROE, CFROIC, LTDE, CapAcqRatio, and ShareChg.
This indicator is an equal weighted combination of the following valuation indicators: BP, FCFP, EBITDAEV, EP, DivP, SEV.
This indicator is an equal weighted combination of the following earnings quality factors: CashCycle, NetProfitMargin, WCAccruals, AccrualRatioCF, NIStab.
This indicator is a combination of the following size factors: LogMktCap, LogTTMSales
This indicator is an equal weighted combination of the following volatility factors: AnnVol12M, AnnVol1M, 60MBeta, 90DCV.
This indicator is an equal weighted combination of the following analyst expectation factors: LTG, EstDiff, SUE, and EPSNumRevFY1.

factorname: Adj Forward Free Cash Flow to Price Ratio
factordefinition: This valuation ratio compares the company's forward looking annual free cash flow to its market value. Generally, the lower this ratio is, the more expensive the company is.
The ratio of consensus estimates for the next year's earnings to the current stock price.

factorname: Forward Free Cash Flow to Price Ratio
factordefinition: The ratio of the consensus forecast of annual free cash flow to the current market value of equity.

The difference between realized quarterly earnings per share and the consensus estimate, relative the prior day's closing price. *Note that price denominator is fixed at time of announcement and does not change until then next earnings release
The ratio of the standard deviation of analysts' EPS estimates for FY1 to the absolute value of the mean estimate.

The difference between realized quarterly earnings per share and the consensus estimate , relative to the standard deviation of the past differences.  For US & Canada, Normalized EPS is used; for ex-NA, we use GAAP EPS.

factorname: Adjusted Number of EPS FY1 Revisions
factordefinition: This factor represents the number of positive 1 month revisions minus number of negative 1 month revisions in a company's FY1 EPS estimates.  For FY1 estimates, this factor uses data from the daily estimates file, but uses data from the monthly estimate file if data is not available in the daily file.

The ratio of the sum of consensus estimates of quarterly earnings per share for the next four quarters to the current stock price, multiplied by the consensus estimate of long-term growth in earnings per share.
The ratio of the standard deviation of analysts' EPS estimates for FY2 to the absolute value of the mean estimate.

The factor is weighted average of number of net upward 1 month revisions in consensus estimate of FY1 earnings per share in current month, and the number of net upward 1 month revisions in the previous month.
This metric compares the company's forward annual earnings to its current market price.

factorname: Adjusted 3M Revision in FY1 EPS Estimate
factordefinition: The factor measures the last 3 month changes in analyst average earnings estimate for Fiscal Year 1, adjusted by most recent stock price.  For FY1 estimates, this factor uses data from the daily estimates file, but uses data from the monthly estimate file if data is not available in the daily file.
It's defined as the ratio of trailing four quarter income before extraordinary items to trailing four quarter sales
This factor is the log value of the market capitalization cubed.
This stochastic factor is calculated as the difference between current closing price and low price of the last 20 days, divided by the difference between high and low of the last 20 days.
This factor follows the definition of RSI. It is calculated over the last 14 days.

This factor is the money flow over volume of the last 5 days. The nominator is the 5 day sum of price times trading volume, weighted by the sign of the daily returns. The denominator is the simple 5 day sum of price times trading volume.

For each of the past 12 quarters, we use the TTM earnings to calculate the slope of the linear trend line fitted to the 12 data points. Subsequently, the slope will then be divided by the average of all TTM earnings for the past 12 quarters.
This factor is constructed the same way as Factor  3YAvgAnnSalesGrw. The only difference is that this is a calculation for EPS instead of sales.
We first calculate the 1-year percentage changes in sales, for the past three years. Then, we calculate the three year average of all three 1-year percentage changes.

factorname: Number of Consecutive Qtrs of Pos. Changes in TTM Cash Flows
factordefinition: For each of the past 24 quarters, we calculate the TTM cash flows, and count the number of times the consecutive changes in those TTM cash flows are positive, we count each change as +1.

factorname: 4-Week Change in 12-Month Forward Earnings Consensus Estimate/Price
factordefinition: The 4 week change in the Consensus Estimate divided by Price.

factorname: 8-Week Change in 12-Month Forward Earnings Consensus Estimate/Price
factordefinition: The 8 week change in the Consensus Estimate divided by Price.

factorname: Expected Earnings Growth: Fiscal Year 2/Fiscal Year 1
factordefinition: This factor is calculated by taking the ratio of the FY2 EPS estimation and the FY1 EPS estimation.
This factor is calculated using the mean EPS estimation long term growth divided by 100.

This factor is calculated first by taking the difference between the current TTM sales and the TTM sales one year ago divided by the absolute value of the TTM sales one year ago, and then taking the difference between the ratio today and the ratio 3 month ago.
This factor is calculated the same way as the factor 3MSalesMom. The only difference is that we now take the 6 month difference of the ratios than 3 month.
This factor is the 26 week price T-statistic.
This is the ratio of a bank's non-accrual loans and loans past due over tangible common equity and loan loss reserves
Ratio of all loans past due at least 30 days over the total loan and lease financing receivables
This is the ratio of loans and leases over core deposits
One year change in the ratio of loans & leases past due 30-89 days over total loans and lease financing receivables
The ratio of problem loans (non-accrual loans and loans past due) over total assets
This is the ratio of a bank's tangible common equity over price and shares outstanding
This is the ratio of a bank's non-performing assets to its average earning assets
This is the ratio of non-performing loans and other real estate loans over tangible common equity and loan loss reserves
This ratio equals Tier 1 capital over total risk-weighted assets.
This factor is the sum of the various loan types over gross loans squared
This is the ratio of adjusted operating income over total assets
This is the ratio of interest paid on deposits over average interest bearing deposits
This is the ratio of core deposits over total deposits
This is the ratio of the provision for loans and lease losses over total assets
This is the ratio of a bank's pre-provision profit over price and shares outstanding
This is the ratio of non-interest expense over non-interest income
This is the ratio of demand deposits over total deposits
This is the ratio of time deposits to total deposits
This is the ratio of a bank's pre-provision profit over average earning assets
This is the ratio of a bank's pre-provision profit over total assets
This is the ratio of net income over tangible common equity.
This ratio represents the year-to-year sales growth rate of all stores that have been open for a year or more, as reported by retailers.
The percentage growth in retail space added by a retailer over the last year.
The year-over-year percentage change in earnings per share per minus the year-over-year percentage change in retail space.
The year-over-year percentage change in sales minus the year-over-year percentage change in square footage.
Net profit generated per net square foot of all stores operating during the period.
Sales generated per net square foot of all stores in operation during the period.
Ratio of total number of stores opened in last 12 months to total number of stores in operation at the end of 12 months.
Ratio of total number of stores closed in last 12 months to total number of stores in operation at the end of 12 months.
Change in Total number of stores in operation at the end of the period to the beginning of the period.
One year change in sales growth of all stores that have been open for a year or more.
One year change in sales generated per net square foot of all stores operated during the period.
Residual return from the Fama-French Model scaled by its 36-month standard deviation.

factorname: 1Y Chg in Discounted Future Cash Flows to Market Cap
factordefinition: One year difference in discounted future cash flows (estimated net future cash inflows discounted at a 10% rate) divided by market cap.

factorname: Discounted Future Cash Flows to Market Cap
factordefinition: This ratio compares estimated net future cash flows, provided by oil & gas companies and discounted at a 10% rate, to a company's market capitalization.
This ratio looks at estimated future cash flows, provided by oil & gas companies, as a percentage of a company's market capitalization.
This ratio is the difference between current estimated future cash flows and estimated future cash flows one-year ago, with the difference divided by market capitalization.

factorname: 1Y Chg in Future Cash Flows to Total Assets
factordefinition: A growth factor that measures the change in estimated future cash flow scaled by total assets.

factorname: 1Y Chg in Future Cash Flows per Share
factordefinition: This ratio is the difference between current estimated future cash flows, provided by oil & gas companies, and estimated future cash flows one-year ago on a per-share basis.
The one-year change in the ratio of total proved reserves to average daily production (including oil, natural gas liquids, and natural gas, if applicable).
The ratio of total proved reserves to average daily production (for oil, natural gas liquids, and natural gas, if applicable).
The ratio of the change in total proved reserves to total exploration and development costs (including oil, natural gas liquids, and natural gas, if applicable).

factorname: 1Y Chg in Reserve Acquired to Total Costs
factordefinition: The ratio of the one-year change (difference) in total reserves to total oil & gas costs incurred (including oil, natural gas liquids, and natural gas, if applicable).

factorname: 1Y Chg in Proved Reserves to Market Cap
factordefinition: This signal measures the year over year change in the amount of reserves an oil & gas company holds relative to its market capitalization.
The valuation of oil & gas firms is tied closely to the level of reserves they hold. This signal measures the amount of reserves an oil & gas company holds relative to its market capitalization.
A growth indicator that measures the growth in reserves per common share outstanding.
This factor represents the percentage of annual production that was replaced through the finding or acquiring of new reserves in a given period, as reported by the company.
This ratio is the average price of a barrel of oil sold minus the cost of producing that barrel, divided by the average price per barrel.
The average price per Mcf (thousand cubic feet) of gas minus the cost of producing one Mcf of gas, divided by the average price per Mcf.
This is the log value of the monthly stock close price (unadjusted).

This signal measures the year-over-year change in proved and probable gold ore reserves. Growth in gold ore reserves in general is a sign that a gold miner isn't in danger of depleting its gold reserves.

This factor is the year-over-year change (difference) in proved & probable gold ore reserves to exploration expenditures. This signal measures the cost of acquiring new gold reserves. The ratio's dimension is metric tons per U.S. dollar.

factorname: Proved & Prob Reserves to Market Cap
factordefinition: This signal is the ratio of proved and probable gold ore reserves of a mining company to its market capitalization. The ratio's dimension is metric ton per U.S. dollar.
This factor is the ratio of actual gold production, in troy ounces, to market capitalization in U.S. dollars.
This factor is the year-over-year change in a gold mining company's actual gold production.

This signal is the ratio of proved & probable gold ore reserves to actual gold production. The ratio's dimension is metric tons of gold ore reserves per troy ounce of actual gold production. One metric ton of reserves typically yields a small number of troy ounces of actual gold in production.
This factor is the year-over-year percentage change in the number of restaurants closed over the trailing 12 months.
This factor is the year-over-year percentage change in the number of restaurants opened over the trailing 12 months. Growth in restaurants opened can boost sales growth for a restaurant chain.

factorname: TTM Rest Open & Acquire to Total Rest
factordefinition: This factor measures the number of restaurants opened or acquired over the trailing 12 months as a percentage of the total number of restaurants at the beginning of the 12-month period.

factorname: TTM Rest Closed & Sold to Total Rest
factordefinition: Thia factor measures the number of restaurants closed or sold over the trailing 12 months as a percentage of the total number of restaurants at the beginning of the 12-month period.

factorname: 1 Yr Chg in Number of Restuarants
factordefinition: This factor is the year-over-year change in the number of restaurants in operation.

This factor is the year-over-year change in the sales growth rate for all restaurants that have been open at least one year. Same restaurant store growth figures are provided in restaurant company filings.
This factor is the year-over-year sales growth rate for all restaurants that have been open for at least one year. Same restaurant store growth figures are provided in restaurant company filings.
This factor measures the profitability of a company's restaurant operations, expressed as a percentage of operating profit to total revenues earned during the period.

factorname: 1 Yr Chg in Revenue per Room
factordefinition: This factor is calculated as the one-year change (difference) in hotel room revenues divided by the total number of rooms at the beginning of the period.

factorname: 1 Yr Chg in Number of Rooms
factordefinition: This factor is the year-over-year change in the number of rooms available at the end of the period.

factorname: 1 Yr Chg in Number of Properties
factordefinition: This factor is the year-over-year change in the number of hotel and gaming properties owned.
This factor provides the average total profit per room generated by a hotel and gaming company. The ratio's units are millions of U.S. dollars per room.
This ratio is calculated as total room revenue minus total room expenses, divided by total room revenue.
This factor is the ratio of total room revenue to the total number of rooms at the end of a period. The ratio's units are millions of U.S. dollars per room.

factorname: Hotel & Casino Rev to Oper Exp
factordefinition: This factor is the ratio of total revenue, from both hotel/motel and casino/resort operations, to operating expense, with operating expense expressed as a positive number.

This factor looks at underwriting profit as a percentage of insurance revenues. Underwriting profit (loss) represents the difference between earned premiums and the losses and administrative expenses of an insurance company.

This factor measures the year-over-year change in underwriting profits. Underwriting profit is profit that an insurer derives from providing insurance or reinsurance coverage less claim losses and administrative costs associated with writing those policies.

factorname: 1 Yr Grw in Net Premiums Earned
factordefinition: This factor is the year-over-year change in net premiums earned. Revenue from premiums is one of two primary sources of revenue for insurance companies, and it is generally more persistent than revenue from investments.
This factor is the year-over-year change in total investments. Total investments include investment securities, trading securities, and mortgage-backed securities.
This factor is the ratio of net written premiums to gross written premiums. It indicates the extent of dependence on reinsurance.

factorname: Net Prem Written to Stat Surplus
factordefinition: This metric is the ratio of net written premiums to statutory surplus.

factorname: Insurance: Net Premium Written to Net Assets
factordefinition: This factor is the ratio of net written premiums to net assets. It measures a firm's ability to cover claims with its capital base. A lower ratio means greater solvency for an insurer.
This factor is the ratio of net claim and claim adjustment expense paid to net premiums collected. It measures claims paid as a percentage of net premiums collected.
This ratio measures underwriting and acquisition expenses as a percentage of net premiums collected. It's a measure of operational efficiency in the underwriting operation of an insurer.

This factor measures the sum of claims paid and operating expenses as a percentage of net premiums collected. It's a measure of profitability of the underwriting operation of an insurer. In general, a lower ratio means higher profitability.

factorname: 1 Yr Grw Tot Home Rev to Const in Prog
factordefinition: This factor is the year-to-year change in the ratio of total homebuilding revenues to finished homes and construction in progress.

factorname: Deliv Homes Value Grw to Mkt Cap
factordefinition: This factor is the ratio of the year-over-year difference in the value of delivered homes to the market cap of the builder.

factorname: 1 Yr Grw Tot Home Rev to Inventory
factordefinition: This factor is the year-over-year change in the ratio of home sales to inventory. Total inventories include finished homes, land under development, undeveloped inventories, and deposits.
This factor is calculated as total homebuilding revenues less total homebuilding costs, divided by total homebuilding revenues. It is a measure of profitability.
This factor measures the year-over-year growth in total homebuilding sales, the largest sales component for homebuilders.
This factor measures the year-over-year growth rate in the number of homes and condos that have come under contract during the past 12 months.
This factor measures the year-over-year change in total dollar value of a homebuilder's backlog of unsold homes.
This ratio is a year-over-year change in the actual number of passengers carried during a period. Revenue increases as a carrier flies more passengers.
This factor is the year-over-year change in total miles flown by paying passengers.
This ratio represents the percent of an airline’s total seats that are actually filled during a period. A higher percentage generally means greater profitability.

factorname: Total Profit per Available Seat Mile
factordefinition: This factor looks at the amount of profit an airline generates per available seat mile (ASM). The units of the ratio are U.S. dollars per available seat mile.

factorname: Operating Exp per Available Seat Miles
factordefinition: This factor looks at the amount of expense an airline incurs to support each available seat mile (ASM). The units of the ratio are U.S. dollars per available seat mile.

factorname: Fuel Consumed per Available Seat Mile
factordefinition: This factor looks specifically at the amount of fuel used to support each available seat mile (ASM). The units of the ratio are gallons of jet fuel per ASM.
This factor measures the average age of an airline's fleet of aircraft in years. It is reported by the airline.
This factor is the year-over-year change in broadband subscribers. It is a main driver of revenues within wireline operations at telecommunication companies.

factorname: 1 Yr Grw Net Wireless Subs Additions
factordefinition: This factor is the year-over-year change in the net number of wireless subscribers added. The net number of wireless subscribers added is measured as the number of new customers added less the number of customers who terminated.
This factor measures the number of wireless subscribers as a percentage of the total number of potential customers in a telecommunication company's coverage areas.
This factor measures the rate of wireless subscriber turnover at a telecommunication company. A lower rate indicates a more stable customer base.

This factor measures the year-over-year change in the churn rate, which is the average monthly percentage turnover of wireless subscriber for a telecommunications company. Growth in the churn rate indicates that the company's subscriber base is becoming less stable.

factorname: Number of Patents to Mkt Cap
factordefinition: This factor is the ratio of the number of current patents to market capitalization for pharmaceutical and biotechnology firms. The units used in the ratio are the number of patents per 1 million U.S. dollars of market capitalization.
This factor is the year-over-year change in the number of current patents for pharmaceutical and biotechnology firms.

factorname: 1 Yr Grw Num of Patent Applications
factordefinition: This factor measures the year-over-year change in the number of patent applications for pharmaceutical and biotechnology firms.

factorname: 1 Yr Grw Num of Products in Phase 3
factordefinition: This factor measures the year-over-year change in the number of products in the phase III stage of clinical trials for pharmaceutical and biotechnology firms.
This factor is the year-over-year change in inpatient admissions.
This factor is the year-over-year change in total inpatient days.

factorname: 1 Yr Grw Avg Length of Stay
factordefinition: This factor measures the year-over-year growth rate in the average length of inpatient stays, for hospitals and healthcare facilities. It is measured in days.
This factor measures the year-over-year growth in the number of hospitals and facilities owned by healthcare providers.
This factor is the ratio of total revenue to total hospitals and healthcare facilities owned and operated. The ratio's units are millions of U.S. dollars per hospital/facility.
This factor measures the year-over-year growth in the number of surgeries performed at the provider's hospitals and  healthcare facilities.
This factor is the year-over-year change in the number of beds in a company's licensed hospitals and healthcare facilities.
This factor measures total medical costs as a percentage of total premiums collected. In general, a managed healthcare company is more profitable with a lower medical loss ratio.
This factor is the year-over-year percentage change in healthcare premiums collected for managed care firms.
This factor is the year-over-year change in total enrollments for a managed healthcare company.
This factor is the year-over-year change in a utility company's fuel costs.
This factor measures the year-over-year change in a public utility company's total electric, gas, and water sales.

factorname: 1 Yr Grw Avg Revenue per KWh
factordefinition: This factor is the year-over-year change in average revenue per kilowatt-hour. Receiving more revenue per kilowatt-hour is a sign of growth for a public utility.
This factor measures the year-over-year change in operating revenues for a utility company's electric, gas, and water services. Increased operating revenue is a sign of growth for public utilities.
This factor is the year-over-year change in the number of wireless subscribers for a telecommunications company.
This factor is measured by the ratio of the one year change in ROE over the standard deviation in the one year change in ROE going eight periods back.
This factor is the one year percent change in trailing twelve month cash dividends.
60 month average of the ratio of trailing four quarter income before extraordinary items available for common equity to average book value of common equity over the same period.
60 month average of the ratio of trailing four quarter after-tax net operating profit to average total assets over the same period.
This factor is measured by the ratio of the one year change in ROA over the standard deviation in the one year change in ROA going eight periods back.
60 month average of the trailing four-quarter earnings per share to current stock price.
The payout ratio is the ratio of trailing twelve month cash dividends to trailing twelve month earnings per share.

This factor is measured by the ratio of 5-year average of the one year percentage change in Net Income over the mean absolute deviation in the one year percentage change in Net Income going 5 years back.
This factor is consensus estimate of long-term growth in earnings per share.

The factor measures difference between the number of upward 1month revisions and the number of downward 1 month revisions in analyst estimates of FY1 earnings per share, divided by the number of analyst earnings estimates. For US & Canada, Normalized EPS is used; for ex-NA, we use GAAP EPS.

factorname: US Price Momentum Model - Long Term
factordefinition: This indicator combines relative strength, price, and volume factors over a long-term horizon.
Degree of Financial leverage is the ratio of pretax income and interest over total pretax income.

The metric measures the book value of a company relative to its enterprise value.*Note that EV in the denominator is only updated at same time that fundamental data items are updated, either quarterly or annually.
This factor shows the ratio of operating cash flow to total equity.
This ratio measures the company's profitability by comparing its earnings before interests, taxes, depreciation, and amortization to its total revenue.
This factor is the ratio of current liabilities to price.
This ratio is a measure of a company’s ability to pay for interest on outstanding debt.  This one uses OIBDP rather than EBIT
This factor is the ratio of operating cash flow over current liabilities
The ratio of trailing four quarter free cash flow to average market value of equity over the same period.
The ratio of trailing four quarter sales to average enterprise value over the same period.

Absolute change in shares held by institutional investors to current shares held by institutional investors.Data is sourced from the CIQ Ownership package in Xpressfeed.  Data is not Point-in-Time, for data prior to 2016, a 2 month lag was applied for US companies, and 12 month lag for ex-US.
Recurring (i.e., continued) earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization divided by the enterprise value.
Book value per share excluding intangible assets, such as goodwill.

factorname: Adjusted Operating Cash Flow to Market Cap
factordefinition: Cash flow from operating activities before the effect of changes in allowances for funds used for construction and changes in working capital, divided by market capitalization.

The metric measures the book value of a company relative to its enterprise value.*Note that EV in the denominator is only updated at the same time that fundamental data items are updated, either quarterly or annually.
The factor is a percentage change from a year ago in trailing four quarter net purchases of common and preferred stock. It measures the change in stock repurchases over the last twelve months.

factorname: 3Y Chg in Asset Adjusted Free Cash Flow
factordefinition: This factor is the 3 Year change in Free Cash Flow divided by the 3 Year Average Total Assets for the firm.

factorname: Adjusted 3Y Chg in Asset Adjusted Free Cash Flow
factordefinition: This factor is the 3-year change in Free Cash Flow divided by the one-year (4 quarters) Average Total Assets for the firm.

This metric compares the company's change of operating cash flow to the standard deviation of its last 8 quarter's history. A higher ratio indicates positive trend of the current quarter and stability of the historical cash generation.
